Working for oneself, rather than for an employer.

A spray or shower of droplets hitting a surface.
Not clouded.

Of or pertaining to trees which lose their leaves in winter or the dry season.

An act or instance of putting clothes on.
Any of many plants that produce flowers that are bell-like.

A device for measuring weight.

That which may be won by chance, as in a lottery.
A large cash prize or money.

An eruption; the sudden appearance of a rash, disease, etc.
An outburst, especially of laughter.

The action of imploding.
The tangible substance that goes into the makeup of a physical object.
A high-ranking official or minister in an Islamic government, especially in the Ottoman Empire.
Using one's left hand in preference to, or more skillfully than, one's right.
One who is left-handed.
(informal) One who is left-handed, especially in sports.
(American spelling, chemistry) Any compound of sulfur and a metal or other electropositive element or group.
A craft used for transportation of goods, fishing, racing, recreational cruising, or military use on or in the water, propelled by oars or outboard motor or inboard motor or by wind.

A small long and narrow boat, propelled by one or more people (depending on the size of canoe), using single-bladed paddles. The paddlers face in the direction of travel, in either a seated position, or kneeling on the bottom of the boat. Canoes are open on top, and pointed at both ends.
A type of small boat, covered over by a surface deck, powered by the occupant or occupants using a double-bladed paddle in a sitting position, from a hole in the surface deck.
A small open boat propelled by oars (by rowing).
A small wooden trading vessel, brightly painted and rigged for sail, traditionally used for fishing and trawling.

A ball of snow, usually one made in the hand and thrown for amusement in a snowball fight; also a larger ball of snow made by rolling a snowball around in snow that sticks to it and increases its diameter.
Any of many shrubs and trees, of the genus Viburnum, native to the Northern Hemisphere that have showy clusters of flowers.
The emergency department of a hospital.
A female deity.
Sexual activity with a person of the same sex, sometimes (potentially offensive) restricted to same-sex sex between males.
A person who has been trained to put out fires.
(firefighting) Someone (especially one who is male) who is skilled in the work of fighting fire.
To act as a substitute for a person in their role or office
One who performs tricks (parts of a magician act or entertainingly difficult physical actions).
An athlete who performs acts requiring skill, agility and coordination, often as part of a circus performance.
Existing in or sunk to a low condition, position, or state; contemptible, despicable, miserable.
Excessively eager and attentive to please or to obey instructions; fawning, subservient, servile.
Sorrowful.
In the Mosaic Day of Atonement ritual, a goat symbolically imbued with the sins of the people, and sent out alive into the wilderness while another was sacrificed.

A device used for performing arithmetical calculations; (rare) a table on which loose counters are placed, or (more commonly) an instrument with beads sliding on rods, or counters in grooves, with one row of beads or counters representing units, the next tens, etc.
An artificial passage for water, fitted with a valve or gate, for example in a canal lock or a mill stream, for stopping or regulating the flow.
A board, usually square, covered with such a pattern; especially such a board with 8×8 squares, used to play chess and draughts/checkers.

(mathematics) A diagram in which the relationship between three variables is represented by a straight line or curve for each variable; the value of the third variable corresponding to particular values of the first two is obtained by drawing a straight line through the points on the first two curves that represent particular values of the first two variables and noting the point at which the line intersects the third line or curve.
The state of being collected into a mass, assemblage, or (aggregated) sum.
The fear of wide open spaces, crowds, or uncontrolled social conditions.
The capital and largest city of Corsica, France.
The state or quality of being aimless, or without purpose or direction.
A drug or substance that counteracts the effects of a histamine. Commonly used to alleviate the symptoms of hay fever and other allergies.
Any of the burrowing mammals covered with bony, jointed, protective plates, families Dasypodidae and Chlamyphoridae in the order Cingulata, found in the Americas, especially in South America.
(historical) One of the 15 provinces of Greater Armenia.
To discontinue or interrupt a function, task, position, or event.
Either of a pair of brackets, especially (mainly US) round brackets, ( and ) (used to enclose parenthetical material in a text).
(criminal law) A person who has committed a felony; specifically, one who has been tried and convicted of such a crime.
A list of dramas, operas, pieces, parts, etc., which a company or a person has rehearsed and is prepared to perform or display.
A case in which the uncertainty principle applies; a case in which certain pairs of physical properties such as the position and momentum of a particle cannot be known simultaneously.
A change whereby something goes from one place to another; a state of progression from one place to another; a change of position with respect to time.
The act of equipping, or the state of being equipped, as for a voyage or expedition.
The male ruler of a duchy (female equivalent: duchess).
The sound of steps on hard ground, especially of a horse's hooves.
The ritual act of driving out evil spirits from persons, places or things that are possessed by them.

The state of being objective, just, unbiased, and not influenced by irrational emotions or personal prejudices.

(philosophy) The philosophical system of Aristotle (384 BCE – 322 BCE) and his followers.

The left-wing political philosophy named after and based on the ideas of Leon Trotsky that is characterized by international socialism, opposition to Stalinism, the theory of permanent revolution and the theory of the vanguard party.
A Finnic language spoken in Udmurtia, a republic of Russia.
The act of bathing; an instance of this; the taking of a bath.
The condition of being out of favor; loss of favor, regard, or respect.
